clue.text: Awkward and lumbering in an ugly manoeuvre

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things about, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy blunders through an unattractive bit of driving or parking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe clumsy, graceless movement, which is the plain synonym sense.

clue.text: Strong impulse revealed by our gentry

indicators.note: revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A powerful compulsion is exposed by the behaviour of our upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a strong impulse or desire to act is a craving of exactly this kind.

clue.text: Ceremonial escort's defence of integrity?

parts.note: a guard is a defence or protection
honour is moral integrity

explanation.surface: A formal escort's role is described as protecting someone's moral standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the wordplay, read literally, also describes the escort's job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard term for a body of troops lining up to receive a dignitary.

clue.text: Hard-working American music group taking dip in Asian river

indicators.note: the band goes for a swim after the river, so its letters follow the river's name

parts.note: the Indus is a major river of Pakistan
a trio is a group of three musicians
US is short for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A band from the USA goes swimming in a river in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking dip in' is only a placement signal: the band comes after the river, with the nationality last.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an industrious person is diligent and works hard.

clue.text: Strong desire with regard to reflected light?

parts.note: lust is intense craving
re is the business abbreviation meaning concerning

explanation.surface: A question about whether passion has anything to do with how light bounces off things.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the sheen or gloss of a surface, light reflected from it; the question mark marks the loose definition.

clue.text: Male politician's narcotic drug

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A male MP is linked to an illegal narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis comes from the plant also called by this name, so it serves as a word for the drug.

clue.text: Barker, crossword compiler with UK nationality?

parts.note: English is a nationality within the UK
a setter is the person who compiles a crossword

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker of British nationality is described as a shouter or carnival barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like a person, but here it is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog barks, so a barker is a dog; this is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Quietly ruling, though in the family way

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant

explanation.surface: A queen reigns discreetly, though she is expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the family way is a euphemistic idiom for expecting a child.

clue.text: Lofty duke following senior relative

indicators.note: the duke comes after the relative, so its letter sits at the end

parts.note: a gran, or grandmother, is an older relative

explanation.surface: A haughty nobleman walks behind his elderly relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something lofty is imposing or majestic.

clue.text: Run round hard pebbles on beach

indicators.note: the run goes round the hard letter, enclosing it

parts.note: in cricket a single is one run
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A jogger circles some tough stones on the seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: A single is one run scored in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the small, smooth stones that cover many British beaches.

clue.text: Implicate unfortunate Mercian in it?

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is a mishap, so these letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: An unlucky man from Mercia is accused of being involved in some crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to implicate someone is to show they are involved in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Diversion the frenzied may be driven to?

definitions.meaning: something that draws attention away, an amusement

definitions.text: the frenzied may be driven to?
definitions.meaning: from the idiom about being driven mad with exasperation

explanation.surface: A traffic detour is where maddened drivers end up heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion takes attention away; frantic people are said to be driven to the state of agitated madness by that same word.

clue.text: Obvious friend with capacity to seize power

indicators.note: the pair of words grabs the power letter and holds it between them

parts.note: a pal is a friend
being able means having the capacity
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A clearly capable friend is in a position to take control.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something palpable is so plain it can almost be touched.

clue.text: Have the money for a crossing, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: Can someone pay for a bridge or ferry, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to pay for something is the plain sense of the verb.

clue.text: Come first, keeping most of this inside

indicators.note: the victory word holds the shortened word inside it

parts.note: to win is to come first

indicators.note: the word this loses its final letter, leaving most of it

explanation.surface: A runner finishes top while keeping most of something indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of the printed word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: within means in the interior of something.

clue.text: Comparatively pale and more even-handed

explanation.surface: Someone paler is also more impartial than another.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means both light-skinned and just, so its comparative fits each sense.

clue.text: In favour of case stirring up anger, perhaps

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: Someone supports a legal case which is getting people riled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a law case; it is a grammatical case of nouns, as in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provocative incites a reaction, angry feelings being one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Sailing vessel of some size straddling river

indicators.note: the size word sits astride the river letter, one part each side

parts.note: big means large
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A large sailing ship spans the width of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Person looking through book and software program

definitions.meaning: someone casually leafing through reading matter
a program used for viewing web pages

explanation.surface: A reader flicks through a manual and some computer application.
explanation.definitionFit: One who leafs idly through a book browses it; web-viewing software such as Firefox shares the name.

clue.text: Table part of provisional tariff

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short note about a temporary schedule of charges.
explanation.definitionFit: In a church, the communion table is the holy table at which the Eucharist is celebrated.

clue.text: Bring in vessel mentioned in speech

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the vessel's name gives the entered word

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Someone talks about bringing a container into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in money is to make it as income, the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Amphibian old actor originally rescued in thick mist

parts.note: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

indicators.note: the first letter of rescued goes in the mist

parts.note: fog is thick mist

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of rescued is taken

explanation.surface: A veteran actor is first rescued in a dense mist.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated London actor-manager around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing frog is an example of an amphibian.
